configurePresets.name: gl
configurePresets.description: Portable OpenGL 3.3 backend, with examples, tests and the editor. The configuration to use if you are unsure.

configurePresets.name: gl-debug
configurePresets.description: As 'gl', built with debug info and no optimisation.

configurePresets.name: vulkan
configurePresets.description: Deferred Vulkan renderer: raster G-buffer with ray-traced AO, GI, reflections and shadows. Needs the Vulkan SDK on PATH, or the vcpkg 'vulkan' feature.

configurePresets.name: vulkan-aaa
configurePresets.description: As 'vulkan', plus the AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1 and NVIDIA DLSS temporal upscalers. Windows only; both SDKs are fetched at configure time (the DLSS archive is large).

configurePresets.name: python
configurePresets.description: Builds the pybind11 'threepp' module (GL backend). Add -DPython_EXECUTABLE=<path> to select an interpreter; build the 'threepp_py' target.

configurePresets.name: no-glfw
configurePresets.description: The library without the GLFW frontend. Canvas is the only thing dropped, but Canvas is what creates the context — so this configuration cannot render at all, offscreen or otherwise. It exists to keep the windowing-independent code compiling, and runs the tests that need no window.

configurePresets.name: wasm
configurePresets.description: Web build of the examples. Requires an activated emsdk (EMSDK must be set in the environment).

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-asan
configurePresets.description: Examples are excluded: they are compiled but never run, so instrumenting them buys nothing and they dominate the build time.

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-no-glfw
configurePresets.displayName: CI: Linux, build check without the GLFW frontend

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-vulkan
configurePresets.description: Library only. The runners have no GPU, but the backend and its GLSL shaders still compile: the loader links without a device and glslangValidator needs none.

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-vulkan-lavapipe
configurePresets.displayName: CI: Linux, Vulkan RUNTIME tests on lavapipe
configurePresets.description: As 'ci-linux-vulkan' but with the tests built, so the Vulkan backend can be RUN — on Mesa's lavapipe software rasteriser, which needs no GPU. Only VulkanValidation_test is a cross-hardware gate: it asserts zero validation errors, which any conformant driver must agree on. The pixel goldens are references captured on one GPU and cannot pass here, so the job selects tests by name rather than running everything this preset builds.

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-physx
configurePresets.displayName: CI: Linux, GL + PhysX via vcpkg
configurePresets.description: What the Linux CI job configures. As 'ci-linux', plus the vcpkg 'physx' feature, which is what makes CMake build the PhysX-backed test executables (sensors, play sessions, joints, vehicles, conveyors) and the PhysX example directories instead of skipping them. Needs VCPKG_ROOT in the environment — 'ci-linux' remains the vcpkg-free configuration, and the sanitizer preset still inherits that one. The feature pulls in v-hacd too, which is what enables EditorConvexDecomp_test.

configurePresets.name: ci-windows
configurePresets.displayName: CI: Windows, GL, warnings as errors
configurePresets.description: Ninja needs cl.exe on PATH — run from a developer command prompt.
